Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.clientauth

Class ClientCertificateVerifier

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.clientauth.ClientCertificateVerifier
All Implemented Interfaces:
Consumer<org.springframework.security.oauth2.server.authorization.authentication.OAuth2ClientAuthenticationContext>
public class ClientCertificateVerifier extends Object implements Consumer<org.springframework.security.oauth2.server.authorization.authentication.OAuth2ClientAuthenticationContext>
Verifies the certificate a client presented on the TLS port (RFC 8705), replacing the framework's verifier, which has no trust anchors of its own.
  • tls_client_auth: the chain must validate (PKIX path validation) against the configured trust anchors, and the subject DN of the leaf must equal the one registered for the client. Revocation checking is disabled: it needs a CRL or OCSP endpoint reachable from the server, which this example does not assume. No configured anchor means no client is accepted.
  • self_signed_tls_client_auth: the certificate must be self-signed and its public key one of the keys of the client's registered JWK set; otherwise the decision is the framework's own (which compares it with the keys of the client's jwkSetUrl), whose provider is defaultProvider.
Every refusal is invalid_client.
